mainTopic: A woman who miscarries a שפיר: when does it count as a birth, the argument about cloudy and clear fluid, and the signs of a formed embryo.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an אגדה about how tall certain people were. Then students ask רבי about a woman who miscarries a שפיר full of flesh. רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי quotes his father that she is טמאה לידה, but רבי does not accept it as הלכה, because it may follow רבי יהושע's lone view. That view comes from a ברייתא: רבי יהושע calls even an unformed שפיר a baby, and the חכמים disagree. ריש לקיש, quoting רבי אושעיא, says they argue only about cloudy fluid, while רבי יהושע בן לוי says they argue about clear fluid. The גמרא proves the clear-fluid reading from the פסוק about garments of skin. When רבא challenges רב נחמן, who agrees with רבי אושעיא, the גמרא answers that רבי יהושע is only in doubt and the פסוק is just an אסמכתא. רב rules the woman need not worry in either case, and שמואל says she must, which fits a story from נהרדעא. Finally a ברייתא describes what a formed שפיר looks like and begins to say it is not checked in water, a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How tall the governor of פומבדיתא and אדא the attendant were
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a story about height. The governor of פומבדיתא reached only halfway up אדא the attendant, and everyone else reached only up to the governor's waist.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the governor of פומבדיתא stood next to אדא the attendant, he came up only to אדא's middle. When anyone else stood next to the governor of פומבדיתא, they came up only to his loins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a story from the previous page about how tall certain people were. It gives a chain of comparisons to show how huge אדא the attendant was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is built in two steps. Ordinary people reached only the governor's waist, and the governor reached only half of אדא's height. So אדא was much taller than normal people. This is אגדה and not a הלכה ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the story at the end of the previous page. The new הלכה topic only starts with 'שאלו לפני רבי'.

phrases.english: The governor of Pumbedita
would stand next to Adda the attendant
reaching up to half of him,
and everyone else in the world would stand
next to the governor of Pumbedita, reaching up to his loins.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּרַשְׁתְּבִינָא דְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא קָאֵי לֵיהּ לְאַדָּא דַּיָּילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story about tall people from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדא the attendant was far taller than even the very tall governor of פומבדיתא.

steps.title: Students ask רבי about a sac full of flesh
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רבי what the law is for a woman who miscarries a שפיר full of flesh. רבי says he has not heard a ruling on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי: a woman who miscarries a sac full of flesh, what is the law? He said to them: I have not heard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new הלכה topic begins. The students ask רבי a question, and he honestly says he has no tradition about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a שפיר full of flesh counts as a real birth, which would give her טומאת לידה. רבי does not guess. He says he never received a ruling. That opens the door for someone else to bring a tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: A sac, the gestational sac a fetus forms in
I have not heard (no tradition from my teachers)

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether something counts as a birth decides which kind of טומאה the woman has and how long it lasts.

phrases.english: They asked before רבי:
A woman who miscarries a sac full of flesh
what is the law?
He said to them: I have not heard.
phrases.notes: He means he never got a ruling on this from his teachers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, not connected to the story before it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a woman who miscarries a שפיר full of flesh have טומאת לידה?

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל quotes his father's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי quotes his father, רבי יוסי. If the sac is full of blood she is טמאה נדה. If it is full of flesh she is טמאה לידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי said before him: This is what my father said: if it is full of blood, she is impure as a נדה. If it is full of flesh, she is impure as a woman after birth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי said he had no tradition, so רבי ישמעאל offers one from his father. His father ruled on both cases, a sac full of blood and a sac full of flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling has two parts. A sac full of blood is treated only as blood, so she is a נדה. A sac full of flesh is treated as a birth, so she has טומאת לידה. The second part answers the students' question.

keyTerms.meaning: She has the impurity of a menstruating woman
She has the impurity of a woman who gave birth

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי said before him:
This is what my father said:
If it is full of blood, she is impure as a נדה;
if it is full of flesh, she is impure as after birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an answer to the question רבי could not answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יוסי, a sac full of flesh brings טומאת לידה, and a sac full of blood brings טומאת נדה.

steps.title: רבי starts explaining why he will not fully accept it
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that if רבי ישמעאל had brought a completely new statement from his father, he would have accepted it. The word 'now' begins his reason for holding back, which Step 5 explains.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you had told us a new statement in the name of your father, we would have listened to you. But now...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי starts to push back on accepting the quoted ruling as הלכה. This line sets up his reason, which continues right after the word 'עכשיו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי makes a difference between a ruling that is entirely new and one that is mixed with things already said by others. A fully new statement in רבי יוסי's name he would accept. Because this statement has two parts, he will not accept the whole thing as it stands. The details of why come next.

keyTerms.meaning: If only, had it been that
A new statement, one nobody else said
We would have listened to you (accepted it)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying רבי ישמעאל made up the quote. He is talking about whether the statement can be accepted as הלכה because of how it is built.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Had you told us a new statement
in the name of your father, we would have listened to you.
Now, however,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילְמָלֵי דְּבַר חָדָשׁ אָמַרְתָּ לָנוּ מִשּׁוּם אָבִיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי ישמעאל's quote and starts to limit how far it is accepted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Holds back from accepting the whole two-part statement of רבי יוסי as הלכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The statement is not entirely new. It has two parts, and the full reason is given in the lines that follow.

steps.title: רבי explains why he would not accept רבי יוסי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the first half of רבי יוסי's statement follows a lone opinion, so the second half might also follow a lone opinion, that of רבי יהושע. The הלכה does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the first part (a sac full of blood) was said like a lone opinion, the view of סומכוס quoting רבי מאיר, this part too (a sac full of flesh) may have been said like רבי יהושע. And the הלכה is not like רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי finishes the reason he began with 'now' in the last step. He explains why he cannot simply accept רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי's teaching as the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's ruling on a sac full of blood matches a minority view, סומכוס quoting רבי מאיר. That suggests רבי יוסי may be following minority views in general. So his ruling on a sac full of flesh might follow רבי יהושע, who is also a lone voice, and we do not rule like him.

keyTerms.meaning: A single, lone opinion (a minority view)
The practical law does not follow this opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruling can be suspect if it is tied to a minority opinion, even when it comes with a reliable chain of tradition.

phrases.english: Since he said this first part like a lone opinion
phrases.notes: The 'first part' is רבי יוסי's ruling on a sac full of blood, from Step 3.

phrases.english: like סומכוס, who said it in the name of רבי מאיר,

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָמֵי — שֶׁמָּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: this too: perhaps he said it like רבי יהושע,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the second half, the sac full of flesh.

phrases.english: and the הלכה is not like רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning רבי started in Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating רבי יוסי's ruling on a flesh-filled sac as the accepted הלכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling may rest on רבי יהושע's minority opinion, just as the first half rests on סומכוס's minority opinion.

steps.title: The ברייתא where רבי יהושע argues with the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source showing רבי יהושע's lone view: a sac with no formed tissue counts as a birth according to him, but not according to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: a woman who miscarries a sac with no formed tissue: רבי יהושע says it counts as a baby, and the חכמים say it does not count as a baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי's claim by quoting the ברייתא where רבי יהושע holds a minority view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע treats even an unformed sac as a ולד, so the woman would be טמאה לידה. The חכמים disagree. Since רבי יוסי also calls a flesh-filled sac a birth, he may be following רבי יהושע, which is the view we do not rule like.

keyTerms.meaning: Counts as a baby, so the mother has טומאת לידה

phrases.english: As it is taught: a woman who miscarries a sac with no formed tissue,
רבי יהושע says: it is a baby,
and the חכמים say: it is not a baby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רבי יהושע's minority view mentioned in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע holds a lone view which is not the הלכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute between רבי יהושע and the חכמים.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the dispute is only about cloudy fluid
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש, quoting רבי אושעיא, says רבי יהושע and the חכמים argue only when the fluid is cloudy. When it is clear, everyone agrees it is not a baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said in the name of רבי אושעיא: the argument is about cloudy fluid. But with clear fluid, everyone agrees it is not a baby.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא narrows the ברייתא's argument. It is limited to a sac with cloudy fluid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not say what the fluid looked like. Here we learn that only cloudy fluid is up for debate. With clear fluid, even רבי יהושע agrees there is no baby.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said in the name of רבי אושעיא:
The dispute is about cloudy fluid,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּצָלוּל דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵינוֹ וָלָד.
phrases.english: but with clear fluid, everyone agrees it is not a baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case of the ברייתא's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies only to cloudy fluid. With clear fluid, all agree it is not a ולד.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the dispute is about clear fluid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי disagrees and says the argument applies even when the fluid is clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: the dispute is about clear fluid.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reading of the ברייתא. He says the argument exists even in the clear-fluid case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, רבי יהושע calls it a baby even when the fluid is clear. This is the opposite of what ריש לקיש said, but it leaves open what happens with cloudy fluid. That gap leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The dispute is in the clear-fluid case

phrases.english: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
The dispute is about clear fluid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 7 about which case the dispute covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבי יהושע and the חכמים exists even when the fluid is clear.

steps.title: What does רבי יהושע בן לוי hold about cloudy fluid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהושע בן לוי means that with cloudy fluid everyone agrees it is a baby, or that the dispute covers both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the dispute only about clear fluid, while with cloudy fluid everyone agrees it is a baby? Or perhaps the dispute applies in both cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how to understand רבי יהושע בן לוי. It asks what he would say about cloudy fluid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dispute is only about clear fluid, then even the חכמים agree that cloudy fluid makes it a baby. If the dispute covers both, then the חכמים say 'not a baby' even with cloudy fluid. The difference is what the חכמים hold in the cloudy case.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised (an open question)
Both in this case and in that case

phrases.english: They asked:
Is the dispute about clear fluid,
but with cloudy fluid everyone agrees it is a baby,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא בֵּין בָּזֶה וּבֵין בָּזֶה מַחְלוֹקֶת?
phrases.english: or perhaps the dispute applies both in this case and in that case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what follows from רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to רבי יהושע בן לוי, the חכמים agree that a sac with cloudy fluid is a ולד, or still disagree.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the question open with the word תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No proof is found either way. So we do not know whether, according to רבי יהושע בן לוי, the חכמים agree in the cloudy-fluid case.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי held back from ruling like רבי יוסי because he may be following minority views (סומכוס and רבי יהושע). ריש לקיש says the dispute about an unformed sac is only with cloudy fluid. רבי יהושע בן לוי says it applies with clear fluid too. Whether he holds everyone agrees in the cloudy case is left as תיקו.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean either side won. It means the question is left open with no decision.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from Step 9 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about רבי יהושע בן לוי's view of the cloudy-fluid case remains unresolved.

steps.title: A challenge from the verse about garments of skin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהושע בן חנניה's teaching that God makes skin only for a formed person. This will be used to challenge רבי אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי יהושע בן חנניה taught from the פסוק 'And God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin, and clothed them' that God makes skin for a person only after the person has been formed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to challenge רבי אושעיא's view that the argument is only about cloudy fluid. This step sets up the source, and the next steps explain how it challenges him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדם and חוה were formed first and only then got skin. So for רבי יהושע, if there is 'skin' (the sac), there must be a person inside, meaning a baby. This shows that רבי יהושע's reason is the skin itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded; learned a teaching from a פסוק
Skin; here it hints at the sac around a baby

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא —
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya expounded:
"And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife
garments of skin, and clothed them"
This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשֶׂה עוֹר לָאָדָם אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נוֹצַר.
phrases.english: make skin for a person unless he has already been formed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the open question (תיקו), the גמרא goes back to test רבי אושעיא's view against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's claim (Step 7) that the argument is only about cloudy fluid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע's reason is the skin itself, so it should apply whether the fluid is clear or cloudy.

steps.title: So it all depends on the skin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the פסוק that for רבי יהושע, the skin alone decides, whether the fluid is clear or cloudy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Evidently, the matter depends on the skin, and it makes no difference whether the fluid is cloudy or clear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the ברייתא: for רבי יהושע, the sac (skin) is what makes it a baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If skin proves there was a person, then the look of the fluid does not matter. That fits the view that the argument covers clear fluid too, and it does not fit רבי אושעיא.

phrases.english: Evidently, the matter depends on the skin,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא עָכוּר וְלָא שְׁנָא צָלוּל.
phrases.english: no difference if it is cloudy and no difference if it is clear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical meaning out of the ברייתא quoted in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That for רבי יהושע the argument applies even to clear fluid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן חנניה's teaching on 'garments of skin' (בראשית 3:21).

steps.title: Why would a verse be needed for cloudy fluid?
steps.stepSummary: If the argument were only about cloudy fluid, simple logic would already say it was a baby, so the פסוק would be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if the argument is about clear fluid, because that is why a פסוק was needed. But if the argument is about cloudy fluid, why do I need a פסוק? It is just common sense!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge: רבי יהושע needed a פסוק, so the case must be one that logic alone could not decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cloudy fluid already suggests a baby was there and dissolved, so logic would be enough. A פסוק is only needed for the hard case: clear fluid, where nothing suggests a baby except the sac itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for one side, but not the other)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the law is right. It is why רבי יהושע bothered to bring a פסוק at all. A פסוק is not needed to prove something obvious.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say the dispute is about clear fluid,
that is why a verse was needed;
but if you say the dispute is about cloudy fluid,
why do I need a verse?
It is simple logic!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the source in Steps 11-12 rules out רבי אושעיא's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the argument is only about cloudy fluid (Step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק is not used to prove what logic already shows. Since cloudy fluid is logically a baby, the פסוק must be for clear fluid.

steps.title: Conclusion: the argument is about clear fluid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the argument between רבי יהושע and the חכמים covers clear fluid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the argument is about clear fluid. Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and states the conclusion: the argument applies even to clear fluid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי (Step 8) and goes against רבי אושעיא (Step 7). The double 'שמע מינה' closes the proof firmly.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; we can conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: Because רבי יהושע needed a פסוק, his argument with the חכמים must cover clear fluid, where logic alone would not call it a baby.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this: the dispute is about clear fluid.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Steps 11-13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute between רבי יהושע and the חכמים applies even when the fluid is clear.

steps.title: Another teacher agrees with רבי אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says the argument is only about cloudy fluid. With clear fluid, everyone agrees it is not a baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the argument is about cloudy fluid, but with clear fluid everyone agrees it is not a baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records that another אמורא held the same view as רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכן' (and likewise) links this statement to רבי אושעיא's view in Step 7. It limits the argument to cloudy fluid, so clear fluid is not a baby according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; this matches an earlier view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't be thrown: this line says the opposite of the conclusion just reached. It records that רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, held like רבי אושעיא.

phrases.english: And likewise Rav Nachman said,
phrases.notes: 'Likewise' points back to רבי אושעיא's view in Step 7.

phrases.english: that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The dispute is about cloudy fluid,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּצָלוּל — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵינוֹ וָלָד.
phrases.english: but with clear fluid, everyone agrees it is not a baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to support the view of רבי אושעיא from Step 7, after the proof against it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is limited to cloudy fluid. With clear fluid, everyone agrees it is not a baby.

steps.title: רבא quotes a משנה about signs of a baby for firstborn law
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a challenge to רב נחמן by quoting a משנה. It lists what counts as a sign that a baby was born: in a small animal, a murky discharge; in a large animal, an afterbirth; in a woman, a sac or an afterbirth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: But the Sages said that a sign of a baby is this: in a small animal, a murky discharge. In a large animal, an afterbirth. In a woman, a sac or an afterbirth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up a challenge against רב נחמן by quoting a משנה about firstborns. The actual question comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a mother first gives birth to something that counts as a baby, the next child is not a בכור. The משנה lists the signs that count as a baby. The key detail: a שפיר counts for a woman but is not listed for animals.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign of a baby: something whose birth counts as if a baby was born
A small animal, like a sheep or goat
A large animal, like a cow
A murky, dirty discharge from the womb
A sac, the skin-like bag a baby forms in

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
But they said: a sign of a baby is
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בכורות 19b. It is about which births stop the next child from being a בכור.

phrases.english: in a small animal, a murky discharge;
in a large one, an afterbirth;
in a woman, a sac or an afterbirth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רב נחמן's statement in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the argument is only about cloudy fluid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: a משנה in בכורות that treats a שפיר differently for a woman and an animal will be used to prove the argument is about clear fluid.

steps.title: The difference between woman and animal fits the clear-fluid view
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that a שפיר does not count for an animal. That fits well if the argument is about clear fluid. A פסוק includes a שפיר for a woman, but no פסוק does that for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet a sac in an animal does not exempt. Granted, if you say the argument is about clear fluid, that is why. For a woman, a פסוק included a sac, so a sac exempts. For an animal, no פסוק included it, so a sac does not exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא notices that the משנה gives a sac in an animal no force. He shows this makes sense if the argument is about clear fluid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With clear fluid, the only reason to call a sac a baby is the פסוק about skin (step 11). That פסוק speaks about people, so it works only for a woman. This explains why the משנה treats a sac differently for animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts: here, it makes the next child not count as a בְּכוֹר
Granted / it works out fine if...

phrases.english: Yet a sac in an animal does not exempt.
Granted, if you say
the argument is about clear fluid, that is the reason.
A woman, for whom the verse included it,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about God making skin for a person, from step 11.

phrases.english: a sac exempts in her case.
An animal, for which the verse did not include it,
a sac does not exempt in its case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה quoted in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the argument between רבי יהושע and the חכמים is about clear fluid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בכורות, where a שפיר exempts for a woman but not for an animal, together with the פסוק about skin

steps.title: If the argument is about cloudy fluid, why would woman and animal differ?
steps.stepSummary: If the argument were about cloudy fluid, the reason would be simple logic. Logic should work the same for a woman and an animal, so the משנה's difference would make no sense. This is a challenge to רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the argument is about cloudy fluid, after all it is a matter of logic. So what is different about a woman, and what is different about an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his challenge. On רב נחמן's view, nothing explains why a sac counts for a woman but not for an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With cloudy fluid, we say there was a baby because the cloudiness looks like a baby that melted (step 13). That reasoning comes from logic, not a פסוק. So it should apply equally to animals, but the משנה says it does not.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a sac is never a baby for animals because of logic. He is saying logic cannot explain a difference between woman and animal. Only a פסוק can, and that only works for clear fluid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבא's main attack on רב נחמן's view from step 15. The next steps answer it, so רב נחמן's view survives.

phrases.english: But if you say
the argument is about cloudy fluid,
after all, it is a matter of logic,
what is different about a woman,
and what is different about an animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the other side: the view of step 17 works, but רב נחמן's view cannot explain the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's statement that the argument is only about cloudy fluid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cloudy-fluid reasoning is logic, and logic applies equally to women and animals. So it cannot explain why the משנה counts a sac only for a woman.

steps.title: רבי יהושע is unsure, so he goes strict each time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. רבי יהושע is not certain that a שפיר with cloudy fluid counts as a baby. Because he is unsure, he takes the strict side in each case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think רבי יהושע is sure about this? No, he is unsure. So here he goes strict, and there he also goes strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 18. רבי יהושע's view is not based on sure logic. It comes from doubt, and he rules strictly wherever that applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 assumed that logic must give the same result for a woman and an animal. The answer is that רבי יהושע has a doubt, not a clear rule. A doubt can come out differently in different areas of law, so the difference in the משנה makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear-cut to him; he is certain
He is in doubt about it

phrases.english: Do you hold
that it is clear-cut to Rabbi Yehoshua?
phrases.notes: He means it is clear to רבי יהושע that a שפיר with cloudy fluid counts as a baby.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua is in doubt about it
and he goes here to the strict side
and here to the strict side.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִפְשָׁט פְּשִׁיט לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב נחמן raised in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes רבי יהושע's view as a doubt instead of a certain logical rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע is certain that a שפיר with cloudy fluid is a baby, so his view should apply the same way to a woman and an animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע is unsure, so in each area he follows the rule for doubt, which can give different results.

steps.title: How the doubt plays out for money, prohibitions and impurity
steps.stepSummary: With a woman's בכור, which is about money, the doubt goes lenient. With an animal's בכור, which involves prohibitions of shearing and work, the doubt goes strict. With a woman's טומאה, the doubt also goes strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a woman, the בכור law is about money, and a doubt about money goes lenient. For an animal, it is about prohibitions such as shearing and working it, and a doubt about a prohibition goes strict. For a woman's impurity too, a doubt about טומאה goes strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how 'strict here and strict there' fits each case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a woman, a בכור son is redeemed by paying a כהן. Since money is in doubt, the father does not have to pay for the next child, so the שפיר counts as a birth. For an animal, a doubtful בכור may not be sheared or worked, so the next animal is still treated as a בכור and the שפיר does not count. For a woman's טומאה, she is treated as impure from a birth.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about money is ruled leniently
A doubt about a prohibition is ruled strictly
Shearing and work, which are forbidden with a בכור animal

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'lenient' with the woman's בכור means treating the שפיר as a real birth. Then the next child is not a בכור, and the father does not have to pay. Being 'strict' with the animal means not counting the שפיר, so the next animal is still a בכור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one doubt can produce opposite-looking results. Each area of law has its own rule for how to settle a doubt.

phrases.english: Regarding a woman, where it is a matter of money
phrases.notes: Redeeming a firstborn son means paying money to a כהן.

phrases.english: a doubt about money goes to the lenient side.
Regarding an animal, where it is a matter of prohibition
since there is a prohibition on shearing and work
a doubt about a prohibition goes to the strict side;
so too regarding a woman
a doubt about impurity goes to the strict side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the answer from Step 19 case by case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies different rules for doubt to money, prohibitions and impurity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Woman and animal should be judged the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money doubts go lenient, so the שפיר counts as a birth for a woman's בכור. Prohibition doubts go strict, so it does not count for an animal. Impurity doubts go strict, so the woman is impure.

steps.title: How can he be unsure if he cites a פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי יהושע brought a פסוק for a woman's impurity, so how can his view be only a doubt?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he really unsure? But he quotes a פסוק!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Steps 19-20. A פסוק seems to make the law certain, not doubtful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פסוק teaches that a שפיר counts as a birth for a woman, then that is a clear Torah law. That clashes with the claim that רבי יהושע is only in doubt.

phrases.english: And is he really in doubt?
But he cites a verse!
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about 'garments of skin' that רבי יהושע brought, back in Step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ? וְהָא קְרָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt-based answer of Steps 19-20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהושע is in doubt about a שפיר with cloudy fluid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק makes a law certain, so he should not be unsure.

steps.title: The law is מדרבנן and the פסוק is only a support
steps.stepSummary: The impurity is a rabbinic law. The פסוק is just an אסמכתא, a hint the חכמים attached to it, and not the real source.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is rabbinic, and the פסוק is only a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק does not create a Torah law here. It only supports a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, רבי יהושע is still unsure. He rules the woman impure only at a rabbinic level because of that doubt, and the פסוק is just a hint attached to that rule. This saves רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק used only as a support or hint, not as the real source

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע is unsure whether a שפיר with cloudy fluid is a baby. Money doubts go lenient, while doubts about prohibitions and טומאה go strict. The פסוק is only an אסמכתא for a rabbinic rule. This defends רב נחמן's view that the argument is about cloudy fluid.

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrades the פסוק to an אסמכתא for a rabbinic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק makes the woman's impurity a certain Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The impurity is rabbinic, so a Torah-level doubt can remain. רב נחמן's view stands.

steps.title: רב חנינא asks רב which of four views he follows
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא בר שלמיא lists the views of רבי, רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, רבי אושעיא and רבי יהושע בן לוי, and asks רב which one he holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא בר שלמיא said to רב: Here is the view of רבי, here is the view of רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי, here is the view of רבי אושעיא, and here is the view of רבי יהושע בן לוי. Which one do you, Master, agree with?
steps.whatsHappening: A student lays out four opinions about a שפיר that were said earlier and asks רב to pick one. This sets up רב's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four views do not agree with each other. רבי said he never heard a ruling, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי quoted his father that the woman is טמאה. רבי אושעיא put the argument in a case of cloudy fluid, and רבי יהושע בן לוי put it in a case of clear fluid. רב חנינא wants to know where רב stands in this mix.

keyTerms.meaning: A sac that comes out of a woman, with no clearly formed baby inside
Master; a respectful way to say 'you' to a teacher
Whose opinion does he hold like?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chanina bar Shelamya said to Rav:
Here is the view of Rebbi,
phrases.notes: רבי said he never heard from his teachers what the ruling is for a sac full of flesh.

phrases.english: here is the view of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei,
and here is the view of Rabbi Oshaya,
phrases.notes: He held the argument is about a sac with cloudy fluid. רבי יהושע בן לוי, next, held it is about clear fluid.

phrases.english: and here is the view of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi —
which of them do you, Master, agree with?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth about רבי יהושע's doubt, the גמרא asks what the practical ruling is according to רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the four earlier views רב follows in practice.

steps.title: רב: in both cases she does not worry
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that whether the fluid is cloudy or clear, the woman does not need to worry that she gave birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say that in this case and in that case, she does not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. In both cases, cloudy fluid and clear fluid, the woman is not treated as someone who gave birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not pick one of the four views. He gives his own lenient ruling for both kinds of fluid. So a שפיר with no formed shape does not give her the status of a יולדת.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this case and that case
She does not need to worry (about having given birth)

phrases.english: He said to him: I say

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה, אֵינָהּ חוֹשֶׁשֶׁת.
phrases.english: that in both this case and that case, she does not need to worry.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means cloudy fluid and clear fluid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנִי אוֹמֵר אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה, אֵינָהּ חוֹשֶׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב is lenient in both cases: the woman is not treated as having given birth.

steps.title: שמואל: in both cases she must worry
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and says that in both cases the woman must worry that she gave birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: In both this case and that case, she must worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives שמואל's view, which is the opposite of רב's. For him, in both cases the woman is treated as if she may have given birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is lenient for both kinds of fluid, and שמואל is strict for both. So the woman keeps the strict rules of a יולדת, just in case there was a baby.

keyTerms.meaning: She must worry, so she keeps the strict rules just in case

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
in both this case and that case, she must worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה חוֹשֶׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In both cloudy and clear fluid, the woman must be concerned that she gave birth.

steps.title: שמואל's view fits the story from נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows שמואל is consistent: in נהרדעא they never ruled a שפיר pure, except once when שמואל saw a hair through a see-through sac.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל follows his own reasoning, because when רב דימי came he said: In נהרדעא they never ruled a sac pure, except for one sac that came before שמואל. He placed a hair on one side of it and saw it from the other side. He said: If there were a baby in it, it would not be so see-through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report from רב דימי to show that שמואל's strict view matches how he ruled in real life. He was lenient only once, when the sac was totally see-through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's city they always treated a שפיר as a possible baby. The one exception was a sac so clear that a hair behind it could be seen, which proved there was no baby inside. So the exception actually supports his strict rule for normal cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes with his own reasoning; this fits what he says elsewhere
נהרדעא, the city in בבל where שמואל taught

steps.whatToRemember: רב is lenient on a שפיר in both cases, and שמואל is strict in both. שמואל was lenient only when the sac was clearly empty, so see-through that you could see a hair behind it.

phrases.english: And Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
because when Rav Dimi came, he said:
In Neharde'a they never ruled a sac pure,
except for one particular sac
that came before Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַנַּח עֲלֵיהּ חוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה מֵהַאי גִּיסָא
phrases.english: who placed a hair on one side of it
and saw it from the other side.
He said: If there were a baby in it,
it would not be this see-through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 25 by showing שמואל's strict view matches how he ruled in practice.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a woman with a שפיר must be concerned in all cases.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב דימי's report that נהרדעא never ruled a שפיר pure except one totally see-through sac that שמואל tested with a hair.

steps.title: What counts as a sac with a formed shape?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words 'if it was מרוקם' and quotes a ברייתא asking what a שפיר מרוקם is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if it was formed, etc.' The Rabbis taught: What is a formed sac?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about a sac where a shape has formed. It brings a ברייתא that asks how to define it. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about a sac with no shape. Now the question is the opposite: when do we say a shape has formed? If it has, the woman gets the status of a יולדת.

keyTerms.meaning: Formed, where the shape of a body has started to develop
Etc. The rest of the quoted משנה line is left out

phrases.english: The משנה said: "And if it was formed, etc."
phrases.notes: In that case the משנה treats her as a woman who gave birth, keeping the strict rules of both a boy and a girl.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What is a formed sac?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the argument about an unformed שפיר to the משנה's next case, a formed one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of a שפיר מרוקם.

steps.title: אבא שאול: it starts with the head and two eyes
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says the baby forms first from the head, and the two eyes look like two drops, like a fly's eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: Its forming starts from its head, and its two eyes are like two drops, like those of a fly.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול answers the ברייתא's question. He describes what you would see at the very start of a baby's forming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign of a formed sac is the start of the head. The eyes show up as two tiny drops, the size of a fly's eyes. Once you can see this, the sac counts as מרוקם.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
the beginning of its forming is from its head,
and its two eyes
are like two drops, like those of a fly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A formed sac shows the start of a head, with two eyes like a fly's two drops.

steps.title: רבי חייא: the eyes are apart, and the nostrils look like drops too
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא adds that the two eyes are set apart from each other, and that the two nostrils also look like a fly's two drops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: They are far apart from each other. Two nostrils are like two drops, like those of a fly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא adds details to אבא שאול's description. The eyes must be spaced apart, and the nostrils also show up as tiny drops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא makes the sign more exact. Two eye-drops must be separated from each other to count. The nose also starts as two tiny drops, like a fly's.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught:
they are far apart from each other.
Two nostrils
are like two drops, like those of a fly.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: מְרוּחָקִין זֶה מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds details to אבא שאול's description in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eyes must be spaced apart, and the two nostrils also look like a fly's two drops.

steps.title: More signs of a formed embryo: mouth, body size, and female sign
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא continues describing the embryo. Its features are close together, its mouth is a thin line like a hair, its body is the size of a lentil, and a female shows a line like a barley grain lengthwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: and they are close to each other, and its mouth is stretched like a strand of hair, and its body is like a lentil, and if it was a female, it is recognized by a mark like a barley grain along its length.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps listing signs from רבי חייא that show a שפיר is truly מרוקם (formed).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 28-29 described the eyes and nostrils as two tiny drops. Now רבי חייא adds the mouth, the size of the whole body, and a way to tell if it is female. These signs tell us when the woman counts as having given birth.

keyTerms.meaning: a strand of hair; here, how thin the mouth looks
a lentil; the size of the embryo's body
a barley grain; the shape of the female sign

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught:
and they are close to each other,
and its mouth is stretched like a strand of hair,
and its body is like a lentil,
and if it was a female —
it is recognized like a barley grain, along its length.
phrases.notes: He means a thin line, like the crease in a barley grain, running up and down the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: וּמְקוֹרָבִין זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי חייא's list of signs from step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A formed embryo has a hair-thin mouth and a lentil-sized body, and a female shows a lengthwise barley-like line.

steps.title: The embryo has no shaped arms or legs yet
steps.stepSummary: At this early stage, the embryo does not yet have separate arms and legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it does not have shaped hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more point: even though the embryo counts as formed, its arms and legs are not shaped yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us that we do not need to see arms or legs to call the שפיר מרוקם. The face signs and body size are enough at this stage.

keyTerms.meaning: a clear shape or outline (literally, a cutting)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a שפיר needs arms and legs to count as formed. The ברייתא says clearly that at this stage it does not have them.

phrases.english: and it does not have shaped hands and feet,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the description in step 30: what the embryo does not yet have.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A formed embryo at this stage does not yet have arms and legs.

steps.title: A verse in איוב describes this early stage
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes איוב, who describes how a baby is formed little by little: first poured like milk, then firmed like cheese, then given skin, flesh, bones and sinews.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about it, it is stated in the Prophets and Writings: 'Did You not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese? You clothed me with skin and flesh, and wove me together with bones and sinews. You gave me life and kindness, and Your care guarded my spirit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק that matches its description of the embryo forming slowly, step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse shows a baby being formed in stages, from soft and shapeless to having skin, flesh and bones. This fits the ברייתא's point that at first the embryo is only partly formed, with no arms or legs yet.

keyTerms.meaning: the books of the Prophets and Writings (here, the book of איוב)
You made me firm (like cheese setting)
You wove me together / covered me

phrases.english: and about it, it is stated in the קבלה:
phrases.notes: קבלה here means the books of the Prophets and Writings. The פסוק is from איוב 10:10–12.

phrases.english: "Did You not pour me out like milk,
and make me firm like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh,
and wove me together with bones and sinews.
You granted me life and kindness,
and Your care has guarded my spirit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a verse that matches the early, partly formed stage described in steps 30–31.
steps.raayaObject: The description of the embryo forming in stages, without arms or legs at first.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 10:10–12, which describes a baby formed slowly from milk-like, to cheese-like, to skin, flesh and bones.

steps.title: The embryo is not checked in water
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins a new rule: we do not check the embryo by putting it in water, because water is too strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not examine it in water, because water is strong…
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts teaching how not to examine the embryo: not in water, since water is too strong. The explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא described what a formed embryo looks like. Now it moves to the practical question of how to check it. Water is ruled out because it is too strong for something so delicate, and the full reason continues next.

phrases.english: and we do not examine it in water —
because water is strong

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from describing the embryo to how it may be examined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The embryo is not examined in water, because water is too strong.
